REX DCS/CF: Rapid Extraction Correctional Facility Stretcher
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/rex-dcs-cf-multi-purpose-extraction-stretcher-for-correctional-facilities
Manufacturer page: https://rapidextraction.com/rex-systems/rex-dcs/
Spec sheet: REX for Correctional Facilities brochure
Keywords (Ricky's sheet): Primary: correctional facility stretcher (0/mo). Support only: rescue stretcher (200), rescue litter (150). Jail, inmate, and prison stretcher all show 0. Ricky's note: no search demand for correctional terms, write for the buyer; low volume, high value product (orders around $12K).
Recommended H1 and Subtitle
H1: Rapid Extraction Correctional Facility Stretcher with Restraints – REX DCS/CF
Current H1: REX DCS/CF – Multi-Purpose Extraction Stretcher for Correctional Facilities
Subtitle: Folding Rescue Stretcher with Humane Restraints and Stair Descent Control for Jail and Prison Response Teams
Current subtitle: Rapid Extraction Rex DCS/CF Patient Evacuation Stretcher for Corrections and Detention Facilities
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Rapid Extraction REX DCS/CF is a correctional facility stretcher for jail and prison emergency response teams. It combines a folding rescue stretcher with built-in restraints and a descent control brake, so one officer can move an injured, ill, or restrained inmate across the facility, down the stairs, or out of the building in an emergency.
The tri-fold aluminum frame stores in a small space, is ready to roll in under 30 seconds, and has no components that can become weapons. Humane Restraint ankle and wrist cuffs attach to the frame, and pre-installed straps hold the chest, waist, and legs, so staff can move a restrained person safely and humanely with fewer officers.
Frame: Rugged T-6 aerospace aluminum with a tri-fold panel system
Dimensions: 75”L×26”W open; 25”L×18”W folded
Weight: 48 lbs
Load Capacity: 400 lbs
Setup: Ready to roll in under 30 seconds
Positions: Converts to a backboard, mobile stretcher, or patient treatment cot, and adjusts for supine and Fowler’s positions
Restraints: Humane Restraint ankle and wrist cuffs that secure to the frame, plus pre-installed quick-release polypropylene chest, waist, and leg straps for full body restraint in incline and supine positions
Descent Control System: Hand brake for controlled descent down stairs and steep ground; the parking brake keeps an unattended inmate from moving the stretcher; dual braking rods with an emergency auto-lock
Wheels: Puncture-proof airless all-terrain tires on quick-release wheels
Security: No components can become weapons
Cleaning: Hose-washable
Other Features: Flip-up headrest, adjustable pull handle, protective fenders, and front and rear kickstands
Colors: Blue, Red, Yellow, or Black
Includes: Durable carry case
Warranty: 1-year warranty
Country of Manufacture: Designed and built in the USA
Available Models and Options
REX DCS/CF – Correctional Facility Stretcher: Blue, Red, Yellow, or Black
[H2] Uses in Correctional Facilities
The REX DCS/CF suits jails, prisons, and detention centers that need to move inmates safely with fewer staff, whether the person is injured, ill, or resisting.
Typical uses include:
Cell extraction: Restrain and move an inmate out of a cell and through the facility
Man-down incidents: Move injured inmates or officers to a point of care, from recreation injuries to mass-casualty incidents
Infirmary and medical units: Simple, low-profile patient loading and transport within the infirmary
Emergency evacuation: Bring inmates down the stairs of multi-level buildings during a fire or other emergency
CERT and SORT teams: One officer can do work that would otherwise take several, freeing staff for other duties
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers, Prison and Detention Hardware and Equipment, and Patient Safety Restraints collections for more evacuation and restraint equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
Can one officer move a restrained inmate on the REX DCS/CF?
Yes. Once the inmate is restrained on the stretcher, a single officer can roll the REX DCS/CF through the facility and, with the descent control brake, down the stairs.
How is the REX DCS/CF different from the REX DCS?
The REX DCS/CF adds Humane Restraint ankle and wrist cuffs and pre-installed chest, waist, and leg straps for full body restraint, for use in correctional and detention facilities.
Can it be left with an inmate on board?
The parking brake keeps a restrained inmate from moving the stretcher by shifting their body weight. Follow your facility's policy for observing restrained inmates.
[H2] About Rapid Extraction REX Stretchers
REX stretchers fold in three for compact storage and roll on airless all-terrain wheels, so one responder can move a patient over stairs, rough ground, and long distances.
The REX line includes:
REX ONE: Multi-purpose extraction stretcher that converts to a backboard, mobile stretcher, or treatment cot
REX DCS: The REX ONE with a Descent Control System hand brake for stairs and steep ground
REX DCS/CF: The REX DCS for correctional facilities, with Humane Restraint cuffs and full body restraint straps
[H2] About Rapid Extraction
Rapid Extraction (REX EMS, LLC) of Glendora, California, designs and builds REX stretchers in the U.S.A., and REX stretchers won an EMS World Innovation Award.

Notes and Questions
Keywords: Ricky's primary keyword "correctional facility stretcher" is in the H1, the first sentence, the meta title, and the meta description. "Rescue stretcher" is used as support (subtitle, intro, meta description) and "rescue litter" is left for the REX DCS page, as Ricky noted. Jail, inmate, and prison are used as buyer language, since nobody searches the product terms.
Duplicate content: our current description is word for word the same as the American Detention Supplies page for this product. The new copy is fully rewritten, so the page is unique.
Specs: I used the REX for Correctional Facilities brochure (linked on the current page): 48 lbs, 400 lb load, 75”×26” open, 25”×18” folded. Our current page says "75”x18” fully assembled" and "less than 50 lbs." The REX website gives 42 lbs for the standard REX DCS, so the CF restraints add weight.
Shipping weight: all 4 variants are set to 75 lbs, but the stretcher weighs 48 lbs. Is 75 lbs the boxed weight with the carry case? Should we keep it?
Price: the 4 variants are $3,275 with no compare-at price. American Detention Supplies lists it at $3,285. No change made.
Current meta description says "Government and GSA pricing available." Is that still true? If so, should it go in the description (for example under Includes or in the intro)?
Ricky noted orders are around $12K, so buyers often order several units. Would you like a line such as "Contact us for quantity pricing"?
Brochure: the current page links a 2-page brochure PDF. I listed it as the spec sheet above. Do you want the download link kept on the page?
Colors: the brochure says custom colors are available. I left that out, as with other brands, because we sell the 4 standard colors.
Left out: the US patent number and "6 ft social distance" claim from the brochure.
FAQs: the competitor pages (American Detention Supplies, Bound Tree) have no FAQs. I added three short ones based on what buyers ask: one-officer use, how the CF differs from the REX DCS, and the parking brake.
Images: the 7 current images are kept. Their file names say "REX One Restraint Chair"; I did not rename them. All have alt text equal to the old product title.
